questions.stem: India's first newspaper, 'The Bengal Gazette' (or 'Hicky's Gazette'), was started in 1780 by:
questions.explanation: Hicky's Bengal Gazette — first issue 29 January 1780 in Calcutta. Weekly, English. Critical of Warren Hastings (Governor-General) — Hicky was prosecuted, jailed, and the paper shut down 1782. India's first English-language newspaper, first newspaper of the subcontinent. Other early titles — India Gazette (1781, less critical, government-friendly), Calcutta Gazette (1784, official). Indian-language press began later — Samachar Darpan (Bengali, 1818, by Carey at Serampore Mission Press).

questions.stem: Bal Gangadhar Tilak's two famous newspapers were:
questions.explanation: Tilak co-founded Kesari (Marathi, 1881) and Mahratta (English, 1881) with Gopal Ganesh Agarkar. Used these to attack British rule and rally Indian nationalism. Famously prosecuted twice for sedition — 1897, 1908 (sentenced to 6 years rigorous imprisonment, served in Mandalay, Burma). Published from Pune. Mahatma Gandhi later founded Young India (English, 1919) and Navjivan (Gujarati). Other notable papers: The Hindu (1878, founded by G. Subramania Iyer), Statesman, Pioneer, Bombay Chronicle.

questions.stem: The Vernacular Press Act, 1878 — which restricted Indian-language newspapers — was enacted by:
questions.explanation: Vernacular Press Act 1878 — passed by Viceroy Lord Lytton in response to vernacular criticism of British policies during the 1876-78 Bengal famine. Hindustan and other Indian-language papers were the target — English papers were exempted (clearly discriminatory; called 'gagging act'). Lord Ripon (Lytton's successor) repealed it in 1882. Other repressive press acts — Indian Press Act 1910 (Minto-Morley reforms era; deposit requirement), Indian Press Emergency Act 1931 (against Civil Disobedience Movement).

questions.stem: Match newspaper to founder — which pairing is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: The Times of India — Bal Gangadhar Tilak
The Tribune — Sardar Dyal Singh Majithia (1881)

questions.explanation: Times of India was started in 1838 as 'Bombay Times and Journal of Commerce' by Bennett Coleman. Tilak's papers were Kesari + Mahratta (1881). The Hindu — founded by 'Triplicane Six' (G. Subramania Iyer + 5 others) in 1878. Bombay Chronicle — established 1913 by Pherozeshah Mehta. The Tribune — founded by Sardar Dyal Singh Majithia in Lahore 1881. Other notable origins — Anand Bazar Patrika (Bengali, 1922 by Ashutosh Sarkar), Indian Express (1932 by P. Varadarajulu Naidu).

questions.explanation: Gandhi's papers (English): Young India (1919-1931) — main organ of his ideology during NCM and CDM; Indian Opinion (1903 in South Africa, multilingual). Harijan started 1933 — focused on the upliftment of Dalits. Gandhi also ran Navjivan (Gujarati, 1919) and Harijan-Bandhu (Gujarati). Hindustan Times — founded 1924 by Sunder Singh Lyallpuri (Akali movement); Mahatma Gandhi inaugurated. Pioneer — Allahabad-based, est. 1865.

questions.stem: The 'Press Council of India' (PCI) is a statutory body established under:
questions.explanation: PCI — established under Press Council Act 1978 (replacing earlier 1965 Act, which lapsed during Emergency). Self-regulatory body for the print media. 28 members + Chairman (a retired Supreme Court judge). Issues media norms, hears complaints. Not for electronic / digital media (those covered separately by IT Rules 2021, broadcasting code). Sevanti Ninan, Markandey Katju were past chairpersons. Headquartered in New Delhi.

questions.stem: India's largest-circulating newspaper (any language) is currently:

options.option_text: Dainik Jagran (Hindi) — over 6.5 crore daily readership

questions.explanation: Dainik Jagran (Hindi, est 1942 in Jhansi) — IRS readership consistently the highest (~6.5 crore+). Top 5 by daily readership: Dainik Jagran, Dainik Bhaskar, Hindustan (Hindi), Amar Ujala, The Times of India. ToI leads English newspapers. Tamil — Daily Thanthi; Telugu — Eenadu, Sakshi; Marathi — Lokmat, Sakal; Bengali — Anandabazar; Malayalam — Malayala Manorama. Print readership has held up better in India than the West.
